quest.title: The Flag Still Flies
quest.hook: Hey {name}! It's 1814 and the capital is in trouble. Learn the rule book, test some magnets, measure the escape route, then help Dolley save the day!

Old Ironsides.d: A famous American warship whose sides were so strong cannonballs bounced off.

portrait.d: A painting or picture of a person.

centimeter.d: A small unit for measuring length, about the width of your fingernail.

intro.title: Rule Book Rock
intro.story: Every team needs rules. Our whole country has one big rule book. Learn its name to open the gate!

questions.title: The Constitution
questions.body: The Constitution is the highest law of the United States. It starts with 'We the People' because the people give the government its power.

example.prompt: Who is the boss of the government in the Constitution?
steps: Read the first three words: 'We the People'.
The people choose leaders and make the rules.
So the people are the boss!
Think: the Constitution is the biggest rule book.
A rule book is a kind of law.
choices: The highest law of our country
questions.answer: The highest law of our country
questions.hint: It is the rule book for the whole country.
questions.explanation: The Constitution is the highest law of the United States.

questions.prompt: The Constitution begins with the words 'We the ___'.
questions.hint: Who gives the government its power?
questions.explanation: 'We the People' means the power comes from the people.

questions.prompt: James Madison is called the Father of the ___.
questions.hint: He helped write the big rule book.
questions.explanation: James Madison did so much to write it that he is called the Father of the Constitution.

questions.title: Still working!
questions.body: The Constitution was written in 1787. It is more than 230 years old and we still follow it today!

intro.title: Magnet Marsh
intro.story: The marsh bridge is held by magnets. Figure out which ends stick together to cross!

questions.title: Poles: opposites attract
questions.body: Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole. Opposite poles pull together. Same poles push apart.

example.prompt: You hold a north pole near a south pole. What happens?
steps: North and south are opposites.
Opposites attract.
They pull together: click!
Are the poles the same or opposite?
Same poles push apart.
questions.prompt: Two north poles come close. What happens?
questions.hint: Same poles never want to touch.
questions.explanation: Two north poles are the same, so they repel (push apart).
Magnets have a north and a south pole; opposites attract and same poles repel.

questions.prompt: Which pair of poles will stick together?
questions.explanation: A north pole and a south pole are opposites, so they attract.

intro.title: Measuring Meadow
intro.story: The escape map is drawn in centimeters. Measure carefully so Dolley takes the right path!

questions.title: Measure from zero
questions.body: Line up the object's end with 0 on the ruler. Read the number at the other end. That is the length!

example.prompt: A crayon starts at 0 and ends at 9 on a centimeter ruler. How long is it?
steps: Start at 0.
The other end is at 9.
The crayon is 9 centimeters long.
Find where the object starts and ends.
Count from the start to the end.
questions.prompt: A key goes from 0 to 6 on a centimeter ruler. How long is it?
questions.hint: Read the number where the key ends.

questions.prompt: A ribbon goes from 2 to 10 on the ruler. How long is it?
questions.hint: It did not start at 0! Count from 2 up to 10.
questions.explanation: 10 − 2 = 8, so the ribbon is 8 centimeters long.

questions.prompt: Which tool is best for measuring your pencil?
questions.hint: You want to know how long it is.
questions.explanation: A ruler measures length. A scale measures weight and a clock measures time.

intro.title: Dolley's Dash
intro.story: It is 1814. British soldiers are marching on the White House. First Lady Dolley Madison has minutes to act!

questions.title: The War of 1812
questions.body: The United States fought Britain again in 1812. The British burned the White House, but Dolley Madison saved George Washington's portrait first!

steps: British ships were grabbing American sailors.
Americans said: that is not fair!
So President James Madison asked for war.
Dolley grabbed something very special.
It was a painting of the first president.
questions.prompt: What did Dolley Madison save from the White House?
questions.explanation: Dolley Madison saved the portrait of George Washington before the British burned the White House.

items: British soldiers march toward the city
questions.hint: What happened first, before anything burned?
questions.explanation: The soldiers came, Dolley saved the portrait, then the White House burned.

questions.title: The flag was still there
questions.body: At Fort McHenry the British attacked all night. At dawn the flag still flew. Francis Scott Key wrote a poem that became our national anthem.

example.prompt: What is our national anthem called?
steps: Key saw the star-spangled (star-covered) banner (flag).
His poem was named after it.
The Star-Spangled Banner!

questions.hint: He watched the battle at Fort McHenry.
questions.explanation: Francis Scott Key wrote it after seeing the flag still flying at Fort McHenry.

topics.powerup: Constitution = highest law, 'We the People'. Dolley saved Washington's portrait. Fort McHenry: the flag still flew, so Key wrote our anthem!

intro.title: Fort McHenry at Dawn
intro.story: Cannons boom all night. Keep the flag flying by answering three in a row!

questions.prompt: What did Francis Scott Key see at dawn?
questions.explanation: The flag still flew over Fort McHenry, so the fort had held.

questions.prompt: Match each person to what they did!
questions.hint: Think about Dolley's dash and the poem.
questions.explanation: Dolley saved the portrait, Key wrote the anthem, and James Madison was president.

questions.prompt: The highest law of our land is the ___.
questions.hint: The big rule book from Rule Book Rock.
questions.explanation: The Constitution is the highest law of the United States.

questions.prompt: The Star-Spangled Banner is our national ___.
questions.hint: It is a song sung at big events.
questions.explanation: The Star-Spangled Banner is the national anthem, the country's song.
